stages.name: the register
stages.what: the candidate is in lifecycle/register.yaml as a candidate, with its pin (a digest for a local model), its stage and its retirement date where the provider publishes one
stages.gate: the register and the gateways name the same deployments (lifecycle/register.py --check)

stages.name: the candidate behind the alias on a staging gateway
stages.what: a second LiteLLM configuration (lifecycle/litellm.staging.yaml) puts the candidate behind larkspur-chat; chapter 15's live job runs the workflow's golden set on it through the workflow's own harness and the other local model judges the prose (labs/ch15/ci/live.py)
stages.gate: the gate of E-D9 (labs/ch15/ci/gate.py): no check may lose more cases against the baseline than its threshold allows (the baseline built from the kept runs, until a live run is accepted); the pins are listed for the review that accepts the new baseline
stages.decided_by: the gate's rule; the set's owner reviews the table

stages.name: a canary weight in the gateway
stages.what: larkspur-chat gets the candidate as a second deployment at weight 1 beside the current model at weight 3 (lifecycle/litellm.canary.yaml), so a quarter of the alias's calls go to it; W2's golden questions run through the gateway several times and the cost lines say which arm served each call
stages.gate: O-D12's SLIs over each arm's runs (slo/slis.py): the candidate's success and latency ratios not below the control's on the same traffic, with at least 20 valid runs on the candidate
stages.decided_by: the decision rule (lifecycle/decision.py); the workflow's owner and the platform team read the file

stages.name: promote, remap back, or extend
stages.what: lifecycle/decision.py reads the gate's verdict and the canary's SLIs and gives one of the three
stages.decided_by: the platform team for a promotion; the on-call lead for a remap back pulled under the playbook (O-D13)

because: the gate: trajectory.allowed regressed past the threshold

stages.name: the alias remapped
stages.what: lifecycle/remap.py writes the alias's new deployments into the gateway configuration, whole, and one line into changes.jsonl: the change, its kind, the deployments before and after, who, when, the time to document it, the review, the reason and the evidence files; the proxy reads the configuration at its next start

stages.name: after the remap
stages.what: E-D9: the live job runs again on the new alias map, its result is reviewed and accepted as the baseline, and the register's stage moves (the candidate to serving, the model it replaced to retired when it leaves every gateway)
stages.gate: the review that accepts the baseline (labs/ch15/ci/live.py --accept)
stages.decided_by: the set's owner, with the data and AI center of excellence for the judge's rubric

numbers.waits_for: the live job on the new map and the review that accepts it (E-D9)
